title: Enigma raised $70M to let anyone online control its robots and figure out how humans actually want to talk to machines

content_html:
TL;DR

Enigma raised $70M seed from Index and Ribbit to study human-robot interaction at scale. 100+ proprietary robots controllable online. Founded by Microsoft’s youngest-ever employee and his Unit 8200 co-founder.

Enigma, a robotics research lab less than a year old, is emerging from stealth with a $70 million seed round led by Index Ventures and Ribbit Capital, with participation from Sarah Guo’s Conviction Partners. The startup is not building a foundation model to make robots more capable. It is studying how humans actually want to communicate with robots, on the theory that the interface problem is more important than the capability problem.

To test this, Enigma is launching a public experiment: anyone online can control more than 100 of its proprietary robots housed in hangars in Israel and California. The robots can draw with paintbrushes, fight each other with swords, and perform simple chemistry by mixing flasks. Enigma built both the robotic arms and their underlying models from scratch. The experiment will test different interaction modes, from text and voice to video demonstration to tap-and-drag, to discover what co-founder Jonathan Jacobi calls “the volume knob” of robotics: an interface so intuitive that users do not think about it.

“If you had to do your dishes and spent 15 minutes explaining to a robot where to put everything, everyone reaches the point of ‘Forget it, I’ll just do it myself,‘” Jacobi told TechCrunch. “Right now, everyone is at that point, even with the most capable models.” Jacobi was Microsoft’s youngest-ever employee, recruited by Wiz founder Asaf Rappaport. He co-founded Enigma with Gal Niv. The two met competing in hacking competitions as teenagers and served together in Israel’s Unit 8200. Neither is a roboticist. NEURA Robotics raised $1.4 billion to build physical AI from the inside. Enigma is betting the outside-in approach, starting from the human experience rather than the robot’s capabilities, produces a better result.

The latest rumblings from the EU tech scene, a story from our wise ol' founder Boris, and some questionable AI art. It's free, every week, in your inbox. Sign up now!

The business case is deliberately undefined. Jacobi declined to share specific use cases beyond naming healthcare, logistics, and entertainment as early partner categories. The $70 million seed for a company with no product, no revenue, and an experiment as its launch strategy reflects investor confidence in the team rather than the roadmap. Shield AI raised $2 billion for its Hivemind autonomous pilot, and the robotics funding market is rewarding teams with elite technical backgrounds and contrarian approaches. Whether letting the internet sword-fight with robots in a hangar produces a breakthrough interface or an expensive research project is the question $70 million is designed to answer.

content_html_zh:
TL;DR

Enigma 从 Index 和 Ribbit 筹集了 7000 万美元的种子资金，用于大规模研究人机交互。 100 多个可在线控制的专有机器人。 由微软有史以来最年轻的员工和他的 Unit 8200 联合创始人创立。

Enigma 是一家成立不到一年的机器人研究实验室，在 Index Ventures 和 Ribbit Capital 领投、SarahGuo 的 Conviction Partners 参与的种子轮融资中脱颖而出，获得了 7000 万美元的种子轮融资。 这家初创公司并没有建立一个基础模型来提高机器人的能力。 它正在研究人类实际上如何与机器人进行交流，其理论基础是界面问题比能力问题更重要。

为了测试这一点，Enigma 正在启动一项公开实验：任何在线用户都可以控制位于以色列和加利福尼亚机库中的 100 多个专有机器人。 机器人可以用画笔画画，用剑互相战斗，并通过混合烧瓶进行简单的化学反应。 Enigma 从头开始​​构建了机械臂及其基础模型。 该实验将测试不同的交互模式，从文本和语音到视频演示，再到点击和拖动，以发现联合创始人乔纳森·雅各比（Jonathan Jacobi）所说的机器人技术的“音量旋钮”：一个如此直观的界面，以至于用户不会考虑它。

“如果你必须洗碗并花 15 分钟向机器人解释把所有东西放在哪里，每个人都会达到‘算了，我自己做吧’的地步，”雅各比告诉 TechCrunch。 “现在，每个人都处于这个阶段，即使是最有能力的模型也是如此。” 雅各比是微软有史以来最年轻的员工，由 Wiz 创始人阿萨夫·拉帕波特 (Asaf Rappaport) 招募。 他与 Gal Niv 共同创立了 Enigma。 两人在青少年时期就在黑客比赛中相识，并一起在以色列 8200 部队服役。 两者都不是机器人专家。 NEURA Robotics 筹集了 14 亿美元，用于从内部构建物理人工智能。 Enigma 押注从外到内的方法，从人类经验而不是机器人的能力出发，会产生更好的结果。

商业案例故意未定义。 除了将医疗保健、物流和娱乐列为早期合作伙伴类别之外，雅可比拒绝分享具体用例。 对于一家没有产品、没有收入、只有实验作为其启动策略的公司来说，7000 万美元的种子资金反映了投资者对团队而不是路线图的信心。 Shield AI 为其 Hivemind 自主试点筹集了 20 亿美元，机器人融资市场正在奖励具有精英技术背景和逆向方法的团队。 7000 万美元旨在回答的问题是让互联网与机库中的机器人进行剑斗是否会产生突破性的界面，还是一项昂贵的研究项目。
